canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.name: Vegetarian Mustard Greens and Ginger Soup
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.serving_basis: A pot of soup for about four small family bowls.
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.description: Leafy mustard greens cook quickly with fine strips of ginger in a light, clear vegetarian broth. It is a warming, simple soup to serve alongside a braise or stir-fry.
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.finished_dish: The leaves are tender and the stems retain a slight bite; the clear broth tastes lightly seasoned with fresh ginger.
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.serving: Ladle the greens and broth into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice and savory vegetarian dishes.
tips: Choose fresh mustard greens, remove wilted leaves and wash between the stems.
Add the greens only after the water boils so they keep their color and do not overcook.
Season with vegetarian stock gradually because salt levels vary by brand.
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.image_alt: A bowl of vegetarian mustard greens and ginger soup with green leaves and fine ginger strips in clear broth.
canh-cai-be-xanh-nau-gung-chay.time_note: About 20 minutes; cook the greens only until the broth returns to a boil.
ingredients: Trim, wash well and cut into bite-size pieces.
Peel and cut into thin strips.
Choose a product without animal ingredients.
preparation_steps: Remove wilted leaves and tough stem ends. Wash the greens several times to remove grit, then cut into pieces about 4–5 cm long.
Peel and julienne the ginger. Measure the water, salt and vegetarian seasoning so they are ready when cooking.
cooking_steps: Bring the water and ginger to a boil and simmer for about 2 minutes to infuse the broth.
Add the mustard greens, salt and vegetarian seasoning. Boil over high heat until the broth returns to a boil and the greens are just tender.
Taste, turn off the heat and ladle into a bowl. Avoid prolonged cooking so the greens stay green.

cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.name: Vegetarian White Radish and Mushroom Stir-Fry
aliases: White Radish and Oyster Mushroom Stir-Fry
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.serving_basis: One vegetable plate to share among four people.
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.description: Thin strips of white radish are quickly stir-fried with oyster mushrooms, cilantro and black pepper. The dish is naturally sweet and pairs easily with a light soup or tofu at a vegetarian meal.
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.finished_dish: The radish is tender but still holds its shape; the oyster mushrooms are savory and lightly coated without excess liquid.
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.serving: Serve hot straight from the pan with steamed rice and a light vegetarian soup.
tips: Cut the radish into even strips so it cooks at the same rate.
Stir-fry the mushrooms first over medium-high heat and let excess moisture evaporate.
Cook the radish only for a few minutes; it becomes limp if overcooked.
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian white radish strips stir-fried with oyster mushrooms and green cilantro.
cu-cai-trang-xao-nam-chay.time_note: About 22 minutes; thinly cut radish cooks quickly, so stir-fry it briefly to keep its shape.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian mustard greens and ginger soup
ingredients: Peel, rinse and cut into medium-fine strips.
Tear into bite-size pieces, rinse briefly and drain.
Reduce if the seasoning powder is salty.
Add after turning off the heat.
preparation_steps: Peel and rinse the radish, then cut it into strips. Tear the oyster mushrooms into bite-size pieces and drain well.
Rinse and chop the culantro. Set out the vegetarian seasoning, salt and pepper.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a wok or pan and stir-fry the mushrooms over medium-high heat until tender and most of their moisture has evaporated.
Add the radish, vegetarian seasoning and salt. Toss for about 3–5 minutes, just until the radish is cooked through.
Stir in the culantro, turn off the heat, finish with pepper and serve hot.

cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.name: Vegetarian Napa Cabbage and King Oyster Mushroom Stir-Fry
aliases: Vegetarian Napa Cabbage with King Oyster Mushrooms
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.serving_basis: One stir-fried vegetable dish to share among four people.
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.description: Napa cabbage stays lightly crisp beside chewy king oyster mushrooms, seasoned with vegetarian stock and pepper. This mild stir-fry goes well with steamed rice and a simple soup.
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.finished_dish: The cabbage is just tender with a slight crunch in the stems; the mushrooms are soft and lightly seasoned without excess moisture.
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.serving: Serve hot with scallions and cilantro alongside steamed rice and a vegetarian braise.
tips: Wash the cabbage well and drain it so excess water does not dilute the stir-fry.
Cut the mushrooms into even slices so they cook at the same rate as the cabbage stems.
Add the cabbage after the mushrooms and cook only until tender-crisp.
search_terms: vegetarian napa cabbage and king oyster mushroom stir-fry
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian napa cabbage stir-fried with king oyster mushrooms, scallions and cilantro.
cai-thao-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.time_note: About 20 minutes; prepare the cabbage and mushrooms first so they can be stir-fried quickly in a hot pan.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian mustard greens and ginger soup
ingredients: Separate the leaves, rinse and cut into bite-size pieces.
Trim the base, rinse briefly and slice.
Rinse and cut into short lengths.
Rinse and use as a garnish.
preparation_steps: Separate the cabbage leaves, discard bruised pieces, rinse and cut into bite-size sections; drain well.
Trim the mushroom base, rinse briefly and slice. Cut the scallions into short lengths and rinse the cilantro.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan and stir-fry the king oyster mushrooms until lightly golden and tender.
Add the cabbage, vegetarian seasoning, salt and a little sugar. Stir-fry over high heat for about 3–4 minutes, until the stems are just cooked.
Add the scallions, toss quickly and taste. Turn off the heat, finish with pepper and cilantro, and serve hot.

dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.name: Vietnamese Tofu Braised in Coconut Water
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.serving_basis: One plate of braised tofu for four people with rice.
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.description: Lightly fried tofu simmers in fresh coconut water and vegetarian seasonings until the sauce reduces to a glossy amber glaze. Serve it with hot rice to catch the savory-sweet braising liquid.
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.finished_dish: The tofu has lightly golden sides and a soft center; the coconut sauce is reduced to a thin amber coating with balanced savory and sweet notes.
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice. Finish with scallions and cilantro, adding chili if the family likes heat.
tips: Use firm tofu so the pieces stay intact during frying and braising.
Fry the tofu only until lightly golden; over-frying makes it less able to absorb the sauce.
Taste the vegetarian fish sauce and seasoning powder before adding extra salt.
search_terms: Vietnamese vegetarian tofu braised in coconut water
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.image_alt: A plate of tofu braised in coconut water with a glossy amber sauce, scallions and red chili.
dau-hu-kho-nuoc-dua-chay.time_note: About 35 minutes, including lightly frying the tofu and simmering it until the coconut water reduces.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian mustard greens and ginger soup
ingredients: Drain and cut into bite-size cubes.
For braising; add a little water if the pan dries too soon.
Add only after tasting the braising liquid.
Adjust to the sweetness of the coconut water.
Rinse and use as a garnish.
preparation_steps: Drain the tofu and cut it into medium cubes. Mince the shallots and garlic; rinse and chop the scallions and cilantro, and slice the chili.
Mix the vegetarian fish sauce, seasoning powder, sugar and tomato sauce with the coconut water. Set aside the salt until after tasting.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan and lightly fry the tofu over medium heat until the sides are pale gold. Lift it out and drain.
Pour off most of the oil, leaving a thin coating in the pan. Saute the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then return the tofu.
Add the seasoned coconut water. Bring it to a boil, lower the heat and braise for 8–10 minutes, occasionally spooning sauce over the tofu.
When the sauce reduces to a light glaze, taste and add salt only if needed. Add chili, scallions and pepper, turn off the heat and finish with cilantro.

muop-xao-nam-chay.name: Vietnamese Vegetarian Luffa and Mushroom Stir-Fry
aliases: Vegetarian Sponge Gourd and Mushroom Stir-Fry
muop-xao-nam-chay.serving_basis: One vegetable plate to share among four people with rice.
muop-xao-nam-chay.description: Young Vietnamese luffa is quickly stir-fried with straw, oyster and king oyster mushrooms, with carrot and green peas for natural sweetness. This vegetable-forward dish is a good fit for an everyday vegetarian meal.
muop-xao-nam-chay.finished_dish: The luffa is just tender and keeps its shape; the mushrooms are soft and chewy, the vegetables stay bright, and the seasoning lightly coats the ingredients without excess liquid.
muop-xao-nam-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and finish with cilantro and pepper.
tips: Choose young luffa and cut it just before cooking to limit discoloration.
Cook the carrot and peas first, then add the mushrooms so firmer ingredients have time to cook.
Add luffa last and toss quickly over high heat so it does not turn mushy or release too much water.
muop-xao-nam-chay.image_alt: A plate of Vietnamese luffa stir-fried with mixed mushrooms, carrot and scallions.
muop-xao-nam-chay.time_note: About 37 minutes including washing and slicing the vegetables; actual time varies with the luffa.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian mustard greens and ginger soup
ingredients: Peel, rinse and cut into medium angled slices.
Trim the base, rinse briefly and slice.
Tear into bite-size pieces, rinse briefly and drain.
Trim the base; halve larger mushrooms.
Rinse and remove strings if present.
Slice the white part for sauteing and chop the green part for finishing.
For sauteing the scallion and vegetables.
Adjust to the natural sweetness of the luffa.
Choose a product without animal ingredients.
Add after turning off the heat.
preparation_steps: Peel, rinse and slice the luffa; set it aside and cut it just before cooking.
Trim and rinse the mushrooms, drain well, slice the king oyster mushrooms, tear the oyster mushrooms and halve larger straw mushrooms.
Peel and slice the carrot, rinse the peas, slice the scallion and chop the cilantro. Mix the soy sauce with vegetarian seasoning, salt and sugar.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and saute the white scallion until fragrant.
Add the carrot and peas and toss for about 2 minutes. Add all the mushrooms and the seasoning mixture; stir-fry until the mushrooms are just tender.
Add the luffa, turn the heat high and toss for 2–3 minutes until just tender. Leave the pan uncovered so the vegetables do not steam until mushy.
Taste, add the green scallion, cilantro and pepper, toss briefly, turn off the heat and serve at once.
